page.overview:
What is Dunharrow?

The Hold of Dunharrow, or more simply Dunharrow, was a fortress on a high clifftop used as a refuge by the Rohirrim. It was hidden in the White Mountains above the vale of Harrowdale, between the mountains of Írensaga, Starkhorn, Dwimorberg.

Dunharrow was positioned on a flat upland of heath overlooking Harrowdale, the valley of the river Snowbourn. It was located at the feet of the mountain Starkhorn, with the peak of Írensaga in the north, and the large dark mountain Dwimorberg to the east. The refuge could be reached by way of a winding path known as the Stair of the Hold. This path was lined with statues known as the Púkel-men, statues originally carved by the Men of the White Mountains, in the likeness of the Drúedain. The Firienfeld, a large grassy area for the encampment of soldiers, was right before the stair and below the clifftop. Large carved stones marked the entrance to the Dimholt forest, with a road leading to the Paths of the Dead.

The hamlets of Upbourn and Underharrow lay north of here, in the dale.

The Hold of Dunharrow had been used as a natural stronghold by the Middle Men of the White Mountains during the Second Age several centuries before Rohan, and was scouted by Brego and his son Baldor in the early years of the kingdom.
